title: Care Farm in Western Albemarle
excerpt: Autism Sanctuary is a Virginia DBHDS-licensed working farm in Western Albemarle: meaningful days outdoors with trails, animals, gardens, and person-centered supports.

content.heading: Meaningful days outdoors—with trails, animals, and a community that shows up.
content.lede: A rural working farm on Pea Ridge Road where people with significant support needs spend real time in nature—alongside licensed services grounded in evidence-based and promising practices.

content.heading: One sanctuary today—deep roots in Western Albemarle.
content.body: We operate a single licensed location where people spend real time with **trails, animals, gardens, and people who care**. Days are designed for joy, regulation, and connection—not a clinical waiting room.

checklist.title: High support needs welcome
checklist.text: most people we serve rely on consistent, skilled staffing.

checklist.title: Evidence + practice here
checklist.text: research-backed methods where they fit, and promising practices refined on this farm.

checklist.title: Local first
checklist.text: Crozet, White Hall, and the wider Albemarle community help make the farm feel like more than a program.

content.imageAlt: Garden paths and plantings at Autism Sanctuary’s Virginia farm.

content.heading: Licensed supports that still feel like a day on the farm.

items.title: Group Day & Community Coaching
items.text: Weekday person-centered support in a natural learning environment—therapeutic horticulture, animal care, and guided community participation.

items.title: Residential & Home-Based
items.text: Individualized residential pathways where authorized—designed for stability, dignity, and collaborative planning with families and guardians.

items.title: Workplace Assistance
items.text: Coaching that connects pre-vocational routines on the farm to community roles when that matches a person’s goals.

content.heading: Edgefield, trails, animals, and the Enchanted Forest.
content.body: From cattle and chickens to high-tunnel gardens and two walking trails, the land is the program. Neighbors and volunteers help keep trails open and days generous.
content.imageAlt: Historic Edgefield farmhouse at Autism Sanctuary.

content.heading: Your gift keeps farm days joyful and safe.
content.body: Philanthropy fills gaps Medicaid and grants can miss: trails, barns, gardens, sensory play, and staff development for people with significant support needs.
content.imageAlt: Forest canopy along the Enchanted Forest trail.

content.title: Ready to talk?
content.text: Whether you are exploring programs, volunteering, careers, or a gift—we are glad you reached out.
